metaDescription: Six robot vacuums that listed at $1000 or less when updated, with roller mops and extending edge tools, compared on dock design, mop reach and upkeep.
expertTake: The eufy C28 is the top pick because its 28 cm roller mop scrubs with 24 water ports and its brush is rated for strands up to 30 cm. The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 is the pick for corners, with an extending mop and side brush. Buyers with a small flat should skip this band, because a mid-range dock does the same dry work for far less.
introParagraphs: At this cap, the interesting question is not whether a robot empties itself or washes its pads, because nearly all of them do. It is how the mop touches the floor and whether the body can reach the edges, corners and baseboards that a round machine normally misses.

The cap is $1000, and prices move, so it reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. This guide favours the upper part of the band, where roller mops and extending arms appear, and explains which problem each one solves.

products.name: eufy C28, 15,000 Pa, 28 cm HydroJet roller mop, DuoSpiral brush, auto mop wash
products.description:
The C28 is built around its roller. A 28 cm HydroJet roller with 24 water ports spins at 270 RPM, which means the mop scrubs with contact pressure instead of dragging a damp cloth, and the dock washes the roller automatically. The DuoSpiral brush is rated for strands up to 30 cm, about 11.8 in.

Its 15,000 Pa is modest next to the Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2, and the lower number matters little because the roller and brush do the visible work. It sits at the upper end of the price band and delivers the strongest hard-floor result in this guide. If your floors are mostly tile and wood, the roller is the reason to prefer it. A kitchen with oil splatter is the case where a spinning roller clearly beats a dragged pad.

Over time, hair that escapes the brush builds up at the roller end caps, so slide the roller out and clear it. Wash the dock tray, descale the water lines and replace rollers on schedule. Rollers and brush heads are the long-term cost, so confirm refills exist before you commit. The roller is easy to lift out for rinsing, which is a point in its favour for people who dislike fiddly dock work.
products.bestFor: Hard-floor homes with long-haired people or pets that want a scrubbing mop.
pros: 28 cm roller scrubs with 24 water ports
Brush rated for strands up to 30 cm
Lower noise than the highest-suction models
cons: Roller and brush heads are recurring costs

products.name: Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2, 25,000 Pa, extendable side brush and mop, all-in-one dock
products.description:
The L40 Ultra Gen 2 solves the round-robot corner problem. Both the side brush and the mop pad swing outward to reach corners and under furniture edges, then retract. An all-in-one dock handles emptying, washing and refilling.

It carries 25,000 Pa, more than the eufy C28, and it uses a flat pad rather than a roller. That means less scrubbing power on dried spills, but better reach into square corners. The price sits in the middle of the band, below the Roborock Qrevo S Pro in this guide.

Maintenance is dock care. Rinse the tanks, clear hair from the extending arm mechanism and watch for grit in the slide that lets the mop extend. Pads and bags are the running costs. Replacement pads are sold by the maker and by third parties, and the maker versions fit best. The extending mechanism is the one new part to watch, since it adds a slide that a plain robot does not have.
products.bestFor: Square rooms and baseboards where corner coverage counts most.
pros: Side brush and mop both extend into corners
All-in-one dock empties, washes and refills
cons: Flat pad scrubs less than a roller
Pads and bags are ongoing parts

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S5V, 12,000 Pa, FlexiArm edge mop, warm-air drying dock, dual zero-tangle
products.description:
The Qrevo S5V pairs an extending FlexiArm edge mop with a dock that dries the pads in warm air. A brushless HyperForce motor gives 12,000 Pa, smart obstacle sensing steers around clutter and a dual zero-tangle system keeps hair off the rollers.

Its 12,000 Pa is the lowest suction label in the group, and the price is the highest in the band, which is odd until you note what the money buys: the FlexiArm and the drying dock. Compared with the Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 it has less suction but a more mature app and parts supply. The warm-air drying stage is the quiet feature that stops pads from smelling after a few days. It suits hard-floor homes that value fresh pads.

Expect the usual dock chores: empty the dirty tank, wipe the tray and descale. A weekly glance at the drain screen prevents the slow flow that ends in an error code. Warm-air drying helps, but a dock left wet for days still develops a smell.
products.bestFor: Hard-floor homes that want edge reach and dry pads.
cons: Lowest suction label in the group

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S Pro, 18,500 Pa, 167 F hot-wash dock, anti-tangle
products.description:
The Qrevo S Pro is the plain, strong hot-wash dock. It empties the bin, washes mop pads with 167 F water and refills the clean tank, with a zero-tangle brush system for pet homes. A pad that sees hot water between runs stays much fresher.

Within this band it undercuts the Qrevo S5V and has more suction, 18,500 Pa against 12,000 Pa, but it lacks the FlexiArm edge mop. It is the cleanest answer for a house that mops weekly and does not need extending tools. The hot rinse is also gentler on pad fabric over time than a hot-air dry alone.

Wipe the wash tray weekly, rinse the dirty tank after each mop run and descale in hard-water areas. Replace pads and bags on schedule. Keep a log of the install dates so you can see how long they last in your home.
products.bestFor: Houses that mop weekly and want the strongest pad wash.
cons: Pads and bags are ongoing costs

products.name: Shark AI Ultra AV2501S, Matrix Clean, home mapping, 30-day HEPA bagless base
products.description:
The AV2501S is the dry-cleaning outlier at this cap. Matrix Clean makes several grid passes, home mapping steers it room by room and a bagless base with true HEPA filtration holds up to 30 days. There is no mop at all.

It costs a fraction of the other picks and is the best fit for carpeted homes that do not mop with a robot. Compared with the eufy C28 it has no wet cleaning and a shorter dock interval. If your floors are carpet, it is the sensible way to spend a fraction of the cap. The saved money buys a very good handheld for stairs and furniture.

Empty the base roughly monthly, wash the HEPA filter by the maker schedule and clear the brush ends weekly.
products.bestFor: Carpeted homes that mop by hand.
pros: Far lower price than the mop docks

products.name: iMartine, 18,000 Pa, LiDAR with SLAM, 1.3 L bagless dock, multi-map
products.description:
The iMartine shows how little of the cap many buyers need. LiDAR with SLAM maps the home, multi-map storage supports several floors and a bagless 1.3 L base empties for about 45 days.

Its 18,000 Pa sits between the Qrevo S5V and the Qrevo S Pro, and it costs far less than either. The compromise is brand maturity and a Tuya app that routes control through a third-party cloud. It suits a multi-floor home on a budget. Check the map count on the maker page before relying on it for three levels.

Empty the cup outdoors if possible, rinse the filter and clear the brush ends. Keep the mop pad off rugs. Because the app uses a third-party cloud, create the account with a dedicated address.
products.bestFor: Multi-floor homes on a budget that want a bagless dock.
pros: Bagless dock with no bag cost
Far lower price than the flagships
cons: Small cup fills quickly on carpet

buyingCriteria.explanation: The eufy C28 uses a 28 cm roller that scrubs, and the Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 uses an extending pad that reaches corners. A roller beats a pad on dried spills, and an extending pad beats a roller at baseboards. Pick by what your floors actually need. A quick audit of your floor types and corner count settles the choice.

A round robot misses the last inch of a square corner. The Dreame extends both mop and brush, and the Roborock Qrevo S5V extends a FlexiArm. Count the corners in your layout, because rooms with many corners gain the most. Open plans gain little from extending tools.

Hot water loosens grease. It also helps pads release hair and lint. The Qrevo S Pro washes at 167 F, and the S5V adds warm-air drying. A cold rinse only dilutes the dirt, so hot or heated wash matters for kitchens.

The eufy C28 brush is rated for strands up to 30 cm, and the Roborock models use a zero-tangle system. At this cap, hair handling should be good on every pick, so check end-cap upkeep instead. The end caps are where long strands collect on any roller design, and a monthly look prevents the slow squeal that signals a bearing under strain.

The Shark AV2501S has no mop and the others do. A dry robot suits carpet and a wet one suits hard floor. Do not pay for a wash dock you will not use. Think about the last three weeks and count how many times a mop would actually have run. Many owners mop twice a month and never need the heated stage.

Roborock, Dreame and eufy spares are widely stocked. The iMartine is a smaller brand. Support quality at smaller brands varies, so register the product. Keep a copy of the order confirmation in case the warranty needs proof. A flagship with no roller supply is a poor purchase. Search for the roller part number before you buy. Confirm the dock bags and pads are stocked too.

specDecoder.meaning: A roller mop with water ports that spray fresh water as it turns. It scrubs rather than wipes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The eufy C28 lists 24 ports at 270 RPM.

specDecoder.meaning: An arm that extends the mop toward corners and baseboards. It improves edge coverage.
A pad that swings out past the body. It reaches under furniture edges.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 extends both mop and side brush.

specDecoder.meaning: A base that washes pads with heated water. It cuts odor and streaks.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Qrevo S Pro washes at 167 F.

specDecoder.meaning: A maximum motor rating. It is not comparable across brands.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Dreame lists 25,000 Pa and the Qrevo S5V lists 12,000 Pa.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mop mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rollers, extending pads and FlexiArm. The eufy C28 leads on scrubbing, and the Dreame and Roborock models lead on reach. Dry-only models were judged separately.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dock function
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared washing, drying and emptying. The Qrevo S Pro and S5V lead on washing. The Shark base is dry only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brush design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hair ratings and zero-tangle designs. Maker ratings are claims, so we paid more attention to design than to the number. The eufy C28 states 30 cm strands. The Roborock models use dual systems.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value within the band
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared what each pick delivers for its tier. The iMartine and Shark deliver the most per unit of cost. The flagships deliver the most capability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed repeated owner reports on roller wear, dock smell and app issues. Patterns outweighed single remarks. Models with repeated roller complaints were marked down. Complaints about a squeaking or lopsided roller after six months were treated as a design warning. Streaking and a sour smell from a roller left damp were the commonest.

cards.label: Roller
cards.text: The eufy C28 scrubs with a 28 cm roller. It handles dried spills best and the roller is a wear part.

cards.label: Extending pad
cards.text: The Dreame L40 and Roborock S5V reach corners. They scrub less but cover edges better.

howToChoose.note: Pick the roller for sticky floors and the extending pad for square rooms. Many households end up with the roller and a hand tool for the last inch of corners.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An extending mop or arm, edge mopping that follows the wall and a side brush that sweeps toward the body. Test on your own hallway. Look at the last inch beside the baseboard after the first run.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 extends both mop and brush, and the Qrevo S5V extends a FlexiArm. The eufy C28 relies on its roller.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You mop weekly and have square rooms. The top of the band adds roller or reach.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly vacuum. The Shark AV2501S or iMartine cost far less.

maintenance.why: Grime dries into a film. Rinse and dry it. Standing the roller upright on a rack lets air reach every face.
A film collects and smells. A damp cloth clears it. Use a soft brush for the corners where the tray meets the wall.
Standing grey water sours. Leave the lid open to dry. A fan on the dock for an hour after a mop run also helps.
Grit slows the slide. Wipe and check it moves freely. If it sticks, a drop of water on a cloth is enough to free grit.
Hard water scales pumps. Use the maker descaler. White vinegar is not recommended by every maker, so read the manual first.

faq.q: What does $1000 buy that a lower cap does not?
faq.a: Roller mops, extending arms and warm-air drying. The eufy C28, Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 and Roborock Qrevo S5V show them. Basic docks still handle dry work for less.

They move often. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. Check the live price before buying. Sales events are the best time to buy a flagship. Treat the cap as a snapshot rather than a promise.

faq.q: Is a roller mop better than a pad?
faq.a: For dried spills, yes. A roller scrubs and a pad wipes. A roller is a wear part that needs replacing. Plan on a new roller roughly once a year with weekly mopping.
Only if corners and baseboards matter to you. Square rooms benefit most. Open plans gain little. They are a better fit for a roller that scrubs the open middle of a room.

faq.q: Is the highest suction label worth it?
faq.a: Not alone. Brush, roller and edge reach matter more. A robot with a modest number and a good roller will leave a cleaner floor. A peak Pa number is a poor guide.
Yes. The Shark AV2501S is dry only and suits carpet. Pair it with a hand mop. A flat microfibre mop is cheap and covers the occasional spill on a hard floor.
